page: Amazon Web Services a1.large is a first-generation Arm-based virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and AWS Graviton processors. It features 2 dedicated physical cores running on 64-bit ARMv8 Cortex-A72 microarchitecture clocked at 2.3 GHz with 1 thread per core. The instance provides 4.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and does not include bundled local storage or hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results reflect the limitations of early Arm cloud silicon. The Cortex-A72 cores produce a moderate stress-ng single-core score of 1489.88, but overall multi-threaded and compute-intensive output ranks in lower percentiles, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 700.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 785.09. Memory throughput is constrained, registering 11.18 GB/sec for large block read operations and 6.69 GB/sec for write operations. Cryptographic throughput benefits from dedicated hardware AES support, though absence of vector extensions limits floating-point and matrix computations.

Without local storage, the instance relies entirely on network-attached storage volumes for operational disk I/O. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation makes the instance structurally suitable for lightweight container deployment, basic web servers, and staging environments targeting Arm architecture rather than high-performance computation or memory-bound database engines.
description: Amazon Web Services a1.large is an entry-tier, Arm-based instance powered by the first-generation AWS Graviton processor on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 2 dedicated 64-bit Cortex-A72 cores at 2.3 GHz, 4.0 GB of system RAM, and 1 Gbps baseline network capacity, it operates without local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations show entry-level execution across CPU, memory bandwidth, and database operations, reflecting the early Cortex-A72 architecture. The instance offers a cost-effective, dedicated-core hardware profile tailored for low-intensity Arm64 workloads, lightweight containerized microservices, build environments, and basic static web hosting.
